name: Carthage
summary: A Phoenician trading city in modern Tunisia that built a sea empire across the western Mediterranean and fought Rome in the three Punic Wars.

location.value: Carthage, near modern Tunis, plus ports in Sicily, Sardinia, Spain and North Africa.

terrain.value: A coastal peninsula with fertile farmland inland.

climate.value: Mediterranean: hot dry summers and mild wet winters, good for olives, vines and grain.

resources.value: Farmland, Spanish silver and the purple dye trade.

population.value: 3.7–4.3 million in the empire (222 BCE, infobox); the city itself had perhaps about 250,000.

urbanisation.value: Carthage was one of the largest cities of the Mediterranean.

disease.value: Plague struck Carthaginian armies besieging Syracuse in Sicily (396 BCE).

migration.value: Founded by settlers from Tyre in Phoenicia; later absorbed Libyan, Numidian and Greek people.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

economicBase.value: Sea trade backed by a large navy, plus farming.

tradeRoutes.value: The western Mediterranean and Atlantic coast, explored by Hanno and Himilco.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Carthaginian coins in gold, silver and bronze from the 4th century BCE; tribute from Libyan farmers.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

inequality.value: A wealthy merchant and landowning oligarchy ruled; Libyan farmers paid heavy tribute.

governmentType.value: Monarchy until the 6th century BCE, then an oligarchic republic led by two suffetes.

keyRulers.value: Mago (6th century BCE), Hamilcar Barca, Hasdrubal, Hannibal Barca (general, later suffete).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

succession.value: Two elected chief magistrates (suffetes) each year, with a council of elders and a popular assembly.

institutions.value: A senate and a Court of One Hundred and Four.

stability.value: Generally stable as a republic, but shaken by the Mercenary War (241–238 BCE) after the First Punic War.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between the Barcid family and other factions.

armyAndTech.value: A strong navy and mercenary armies, including war elephants.

majorWars.value: The Sicilian Wars and the three Punic Wars (264–146 BCE).

territoryChange.value: Lost Sicily (241 BCE) and Sardinia to Rome, rebuilt power in Spain, then lost Spain (206 BCE).
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

alliancesRivals.value: Long rivalry with the Greek cities of Sicily, then three wars with Rome; allied at times with Numidian kings.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

scienceEducation.value: Mago’s treatise on agriculture, later translated into Latin.

openness.value: A mixed Phoenician, Berber and Greek culture; Carthaginians traded with everyone in the western Mediterranean.

communicationTransport.value: A great navy and merchant fleet; the Cothon, a circular military harbour; trading posts across the western Mediterranean.

religion.value: Punic religion centred on Baal Hammon and the goddess Tanit; the tophet sanctuaries are debated by historians.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

languageWriting.value: Punic, a Phoenician dialect written in the Phoenician alphabet; Greek was also used in trade.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

artsArchitecture.value: The circular military harbour (the Cothon), tall apartment houses, and Punic masks and jewellery.

socialStructure.value: Merchants and landowners, citizens, Libyan farmers and slaves.

sharedIdentity.value: Phoenician (Punic) heritage, religion and language, shared with colonies across the western Mediterranean.

dailyLife.value: Multi-storey stone houses with plastered walls and drains; bread, olives, fish, figs and the punic porridge (puls punica).

neighbours.value: Rome, the Greek cities of Sicily (Syracuse), Numidia, Iberian peoples and Egypt.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

ideasReligions.value: Spread Phoenician culture around the western Mediterranean.

colonisation.value: Founded colonies across the western Mediterranean.

riseSignals.value: Independence from Tyre in the mid-6th century BCE and a growing trade network.

peakPeriod.value: The 4th–3rd centuries BCE, when Carthage dominated western Mediterranean trade before the First Punic War.

declineSignals.value: Defeat by Rome at Zama (202 BCE) and harsh peace terms.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Ancient Carthage (checked 6 Nov 2026); Miles, Carthage Must Be Destroyed (2010)

outcome.value: Destroyed by Rome in 146 BCE; its land became the Roman province of Africa.

sources.value: Greek and Roman writers (Polybius, Livy) and archaeology. Checked against Wikipedia (“Ancient Carthage”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. Mostly seen through Roman eyes; the founding date is unknown.

knownFor.label: Hannibal crosses the Alps
knownFor.note: Hannibal led an army with war elephants into Italy.

knownFor.label: Tyrian purple dye
knownFor.note: A rare purple dye from sea snails, a Phoenician speciality.
